items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Rod had gotten me and there was going to be a trio, and he got this Jimmy Butts, bass player. And so we made a record for Bob Thiele.

ctx.x: I knew Rod in Chicago, but now we got rather thick. And so -- and Bob Thiele was his man. Bob Theal thought Rod was the greatest.

And so he decided to record on this jazz label. And Rod had gotten me and there was going to be a trio, and he got this Jimmy Butts, bass player. And so we made a record for Bob Thiele. Now, it was after that that Don Qualey decided to record George Zack. And again, the story, he's got George all ready, he stayed with him the night before, he's just glued to him. And now they're in Ross' Tavern, or some tavern, having a drink, because George has to have atmosphere, he can't go up there in that cold studio. And he…

tell you what, we'll have three drinks, and then we go, okay? George says, okay, that'll be fine. So they had the first, they had the second, they order the third, and Qualey says, I'm going to the phone to call the studio and tell them that we're coming. George says, that's fine.
